Every parcel of land is claimed and society has decided it can determine its use better than hunter-gatherers can. Those that are idle but not in poverty do not necessarily turn to crime. A Basic Income would also spur high velocity spending (rather than low-velocity investing) to help get the economy going again and hopefully spur innovation via aggregate demand instead of the tried and anemic supply-side controls of the fed interest rates.

The economic climate today, like the economic climate of early 20th century, is that technology is replacing jobs rapidly, far faster than any kind of "job creation" can keep up. Trains might create jobs, and so do cell phones. But we need to keep the scale in mind and the scales simply don't compare. We already admitted once before that we cannot create enough jobs, thus job rationing. Japan and South Korea have yet to embrace this idea and Japan is in a decades long recession as a result. Europe overall has embraced a different worklife balance.

The economy is very much demand driven. People demand goods, and thus those goods get made. With a poor working class, they have no power to demand anything and thus goods aren't getting made and this removes the total number of jobs. The simplest solution is to simply give them money. This isn't as absurd as it sounds when you realize that we already give money away to big banks via 0% (or in Europe and Japan, negative!) interest rates, or via race-to-the-bottom tax breaks to lure big companies (Walmart loves these and takes huge advantage), or via contracts for goods we don't even need, like the huge order of 1000+ tanks the Army didn't even want. If you want to whine about welfare queens, corporations are the biggest welfare queens of them all.

Moving the subject back to people, the biggest flaw in current welfare programs is welfare cliffs. The laziness among welfare recipients is because they are punished for earning more via insane clawback rates. Tapering assistance off sounds like a good idea until people are in that position and they realize they can make almost the same amount of money for considerably less effort. Or in some cases they earn more money by not working as work incurs transportation and other costs which are poorly accounted for in clawback rates. And this is entirely by design because it's supposed to keep them poor rather than truly lift them out of poverty. Basic income would fix this by changing the mentality about who it is given to and how it is handled by treating it like any other income, and thus eliminating the insane clawback rates. Another note is that "basic income" refers to the requirements for earning it, not the level. As a country's GDP per capita increases, so should each citizens Basic Income. Perhaps in the future where every job is automated and AI does most of the work, each citizen could claim a (in 2017 dollars) $200k Basic Income check.
